old_title: Ukraine war live: Kyiv agrees not to strike Russia amid CIA chief's mysterious visit
new_title: Ukraine war live: New details of CIA chief's Kremlin trip emerge as Trump comments
old_text:
Ukraine heeded a special request from the Donald Trump administration not to attack major Russian cities during a visit by CIA director John Ratcliffe.
The US contacted Kyiv last week to request that it not strike Moscow, St Petersburg and a stretch of northern Russia while a plane carrying the senior US official was flying in and out of the Russian capital, sources told Reuters.
The request covered Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday and was only revealed hours after Ratcliffe left Russia late on Tuesday.
Subsequently, a large US military aircraft was confirmed to have travelled to Russia from the US via Latvia on Tuesday, flight tracking data confirmed.
The purpose of Ratcliffe's visit and the nature of his meetings in Russia were not immediately clear. It was the first known trip to Moscow by a US spy chief since his predecessor, William Burns, held talks with Vladimir Putin in November 2021.
Ukraine resumed strikes on Russia early on Wednesday after Ratcliffe's departure, with Russia saying it downed at least 426 drones overnight.
Russia downs 426 drones overnight, says Russian media citing defence ministry
Russia downed 426 drones overnight, Russian news agencies quoted the defence ministry as saying. The figure includes Russia-controlled parts of Ukraine.
Russia says it struck five vessels in Ukraine's Black Sea ports
The Russian defence ministry said that its forces had struck three cargo vessels carrying supplies for the Ukrainian military and a tanker at the Black Sea port of Pivdennyi yesterday.
The ministry also said it had hit another cargo vessel in the nearby port of Odesa, as well as port infrastructure in Pivdennyi and Odesa and fuel storage facilities at the port of Chornomorsk.
Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region on fire after drone attack
A warehouse of Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries in Russia's Tambov region caught fire after a drone attack, local governor Evgeniy Pervyshov said on the Telegram messaging app.
Pervyshov said one person was injured in the incident.
Ex-US special envoy for Ukraine calls for mobilisation of women
Ukraine should mobilise women in its fight against Russia as they "fight no worse than men," a former US special envoy has urged.
Keith Kellogg told the Naspravdi MAX YouTube channel: "Do I believe women should be mobilised into the army?
"My answer is yes, because they fight no worse than men."
This comes just days after former defence minister Oleksii Reznikov also said that the government should consider a universal conscription model.
Pointing to Israel as an example where women serve alongside men, he said: "That immediately would double our mobilisation resource.
"Then you can clearly see which military positions and specialties can easily be filled by women - they don't have to go to the battlefield.
"They fill many rear positions, logistics and support, and men can be moved from rear positions closer to the front.
"The question is whether society is ready to say, like Israel, that we can survive only if everyone accepts that they must defend Ukraine."
Burnham says he is planning US trip in September to lobby for Ukraine's defence
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he is planning on travelling to the US in September to join European leaders in lobbying President Donald Trump on support for Ukraine's defence.
In an interview with Bloomberg, Mr Burnham said he was "looking forward to going to New York" next month, which is when the UN General Assembly will meet.
He said details of the trip are not yet "fully confirmed" but it is "likely" to go ahead. The trip would mark Mr Burnham's first US visit since becoming Prime Minister in July.
Russia says it downs 426 drones overnight
Russia downed 426 drones overnight, Russian news agencies quoted the defence ministry as saying.
The figure includes operations in Russia-controlled parts of Ukraine.
Two employees of Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant injured in drone attack
At least two employees at the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant were injured in a Ukrainian drone attack, the plant's Russian-installed management said.
The strike occurred near the plant's hydraulic structures and wounded two maintenance and construction workers.
Management did not provide details on any damage caused by the attack.
Ukraine hands Britain 'goldmine' of secret battlefield intelligence to protect bases from Russian spies
Ukraine has handed Britain a "goldmine" of secret battlefield intelligence to help the UK protect its bases from Russian spies.
The agreement was signed as prime minister Andy Burnham made his first visit to Kyiv on Monday to chair his first meeting of the so-called "coalition of the willing" and pledge "continuity" in the UK's approach to Ukraine.
Volodymyr Zelensky handed the Ministry of Defence (MoD) access to Ukraine's "Avengers" AI database, which is expected to help the UK learn from Ukraine's experience on the battlefield and develop AI-powered solutions to national security challenges in both countries, making it the first outside of Ukraine to receive the intelligence, Downing Street said.
Ousted defence minister says Ukraine needs changes to avoid losing war
Ukraine appears to be slowly losing the war against Russia and has a window of only a few months to make key decisions needed to turn the tide in its facour, ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said.
Fedorov said Ukraine lacked any overall vision for how to win the four-year-old conflict, and was hobbled by its failure to innovate.
Ukraine still had "every chance" to win but urgently needed a plan to end the war, he added.
Ukraine's presidential office said in response to Fedorov's comments that he had been positive about the conduct of the war when he was at the ministry and the only thing that had changed was his personal status.
Why is the CIA director in Russia?
Mystery is mounting as to why the CIA director has made a visit to Moscow - in secret - on Tuesday.
It appears to be John Ratcliffe's first known trip to Russia since taking the post in 2025, and it comes at a time when the peace negotiations remain stalled.
Neither the US nor Russian governments has commented on the identity of the official in Russia or the purpose of the visit.
"No, there are no plans for US envoys {travelling to Moscow, " Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters during a press briefing.
So far, CBS News and Axios are reporting that Ratcliffe flew to the Russian capital for meetings, citing unnamed sources.
He personally negotiated the release of a US-Russian dual national Ksenia Karelina in April 2025, and the agency has been involved in exchanges of detainees between the two governments.
The CIA was also involved in the 2024 prisoner exchange that led to the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich, who had spent a year and four months in a tsarist-era prison.
new_text:
CIA director John Ratcliffe warned Russia against an attack on a Nato member, sources familiar with the matter told the Wall Street Journal and Politico.
Earlier this month, the Wall Street Journal reported that US intelligence assessments had indicated that Putin could test Nato's resolve with a limited assault on an allied country over the coming years.
Several possible scenarios had been posited from cyber-attacks to a small-scale land incursion, according to the report.
President Donald Trump said "something may come out of" Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow on Tuesday.
Trump said the US is "working very hard" to end the war in Ukraine, calling the CIA chief a "fantastic guy".
Answering a question on Ratcliffe's visit to Russia, Trump said that the CIA director made a visit to Russia on a "very semi-routine" basis and "something may come out of it".
The Kremlin revealed yesterday that CIA director Ratcliffe held talks with Russian intelligence officials during a mysterious visit this week but did not meet president Vladimir Putin.
Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov framed communication between the two countries' intelligence agencies as positive.
CIA director warned Russia against Nato attack, say sources
CIA director John Ratcliffe warned Russia against an attack on a Nato member, sources familiar with the matter told the Wall Street Journal and Politico.
Earlier this month, the Wall Street Journal reported that US intelligence assessments had indicated that Putin could test Nato's resolve with a limited assault on an allied country over the coming years.
Several possible scenarios had been posited from cyber-attacks to a small-scale land incursion, according to the report.
Kremlin dismisses US media reports that Russia may attack Nato as 'scare-stories'
The Kremlin has dismissed US media reports that Russia could attack a Nato member state and that the purpose of CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow this week had been to warn Moscow against such a move.
Asked to comment on the reports, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said: "A lot of this kind of scare-story material is being published right now. Of course, it has nothing to do with reality and nothing to do with the intentions of the Russian Federation."
Watch: Trump issues first comment on CIA chief's mysterious visit to Moscow
Why did Trump's CIA director make a mysterious short trip to Moscow?
The White House is facing scrutiny after the CIA director made a mysterious visit to Moscow on Tuesday, the first visit by a chief of the intelligence agency in nearly five years.
The US Air Force C-17A Globemaster III flew into Moscow from Latvia before landing at the capital's Vnukovo International Airport on Tuesday, according to Flightradar24.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said he did not have any information about the visit, while President Donald Trump stayed uncharacteristically silent on the matter.
On Tuesday, US media reported that that CIA director John Ratcliffe was on board the aircraft - but no further details were briefed on the purpose of his visit.
Mapped: The UK military bases threatened by Russia as Kremlin rages over missiles for Ukraine
Russia has threatened to bomb UK military bases in its latest threat over Britain's support for Ukraine.
Britain has been told to back off on its hostile stance towards Ukraine by Russia's foreign ministry spokeswoman, Maria Zakharova, who said the UK risked taking the conflict to a new level.
She told the same Moscow news briefing earlier that Britain and France were "playing with fire" by supplying sensitive missile technology to Ukraine.
Ukraine rejects Russian accusations of involvement in Mali attacks
Russian accusations of Ukraine being involved in militant attacks in Mali are fake and not supported by any evidence, Ukraine's foreign ministry said.
"We reject this typical and long-standing lie by Russian officials, which they do not even attempt to back up with any plausible evidence," Heorhii Tykhyi, the ministry's spokesperson, told Reuters.

Russia's foreign ministry spokesperson told the UK to back off on what she called London's hostile stance on the war, which she said risked taking the conflict to an entirely new level.
Maria Zakharova told the same Moscow news briefing earlier that Britain and France were "playing with fire" by supplying sensitive missile technology to Ukraine.
but the Ministry of Defence has hit back saying Russia "should be in no doubt about the resolve of this government to stand against Russian aggression, in Ukraine and against the UK and our allies."
CIA director did not inform EU of visit
CIA director John Ratcliffe did not tell the European Union about his trip to Russia earlier this week, according to European Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho.
"The CIA director did not inform us about his schedule," she told reporters on Thursday.
